Ellen — great to meet you and the FinAnalytics team earlier. Quick responses and next steps below.

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood accepts processor role for the scenario you described (Redwood stores embeddings and token data for inference; FinAnalytics controls the customer data and sends instructions). We'll include the standard processor language in the DPA draft. Please confirm if you anticipate any downstream subprocessor constraints (e.g., disallowing certain cloud providers).

2) SCC modules: based on the data flows you outlined, our recommendation is to follow the EU SCCs: Core Module + Module 2 (Controller to Processor) and Module 5 if you plan to involve a US-based subprocess that will access personal data for support/ops. I've attached a short SCC_module_matrix.xlsx that maps typical scenarios to module picks.

3) SOC 2 / HIPAA: Current status — Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (security) completed June 2026. For HIPAA: we can offer a BAA for regulated workloads on a private deployment, but for your pilot (non-covered entity) the standard DPA should suffice. I'll flag the SOC 2 cert and BAA option in the package we send.

Attachments I'm sending now: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.docx, SCC_module_matrix.xlsx.

Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood Legal) send a DPA draft today for your review (Jonas -> Legal -> Ellen).
- FinAnalytics reviews and marks any redlines — target turnaround 3 business days.
- Confirm SCC module(s) selection once your legal confirms controller/processor mapping.

If that works I'll route the DPA and a short explainer to your team.

Cheers,

Ellen — copying in a couple of practical/legal notes from Redwood Legal to help speed this along: 

- If FinAnalytics is the controller (as indicated), Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) is the standard path. Module 5 is only necessary where there is onward transfer to a third country subprocessor that requires the supplemental provisions — please flag if you have specific subprocessors in scope.
- For your questionnaire items on logging and retention: Redwood's default is 30 days for request logs in hosted mode; longer retention can be configured on dedicated/private deployments. We'll call out retention and audit log options in the DPA.
- SOC 2 Type II: confirmed by Jonas (June 2026). We'll attach the cert to the evidence packet if you want it.

Practical timeline I recommend:
1) FinAnalytics completes and returns the security questionnaire (we'll mark any clarifications).
2) We exchange the DPA redline round (1-3 business days).
3) Finalize SCC selection and sign.

Jonas — please add the HubSpot deal link and any supporting docs to the shared Drive folder so legal can reference. Ellen — if you can return the questionnaire by EOD Wednesday, we should be able to close the DPA before your procurement deadline next week.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
